frame_row: Structural top of the asynchronous Gray-code FIFO that moves words between two unrelated clock domains. It joins the write side, the read side and the storage and holds no logic of its own. The two Gray-coded pointers and the software reset request and acknowledge cross between the sides through configurable synchronizers inside the write and read modules.

label: u_wr
(m_vlsit_afifo_wr)
blocks.function: Write side in the write clock domain. It owns the binary and Gray write pointer, accepts a write when the FIFO is not full and no software reset blocks it, and derives the full and full-threshold flags from the synchronized read pointer, so the flags are pessimistic: they may fall late, never early. It raises a one-cycle overflow pulse for a rejected write, drives the memory write port, and contains the synchronizers of the read pointer and of the reset acknowledge and the write half of the four-phase software reset sequence.

label: u_rd
(m_vlsit_afifo_rd)
blocks.function: Read side in the read clock domain. It owns the binary and Gray read pointer, accepts a read when the FIFO is not empty and no software reset blocks it, and derives the empty and empty-threshold flags from the synchronized write pointer, so the flags are pessimistic. It addresses the storage with the next read pointer so that the output already shows the following word (show-ahead), raises a one-cycle underflow pulse for a rejected read, and contains the synchronizers of the write pointer and of the reset request and the read half of the software reset sequence.

label: u_mem
(m_vlsit_afifo_mem)
blocks.function: Storage of the FIFO: one write port in the write clock domain and one read port in the read clock domain with a registered output. It is a flop array by default or a library SRAM behind a wrapper. The content is not reset. The read data crosses the clock boundary without a synchronizer because an entry is read only after the write pointer proved it was written and is overwritten only after the read pointer passed it.

interfaces.name: Write interface (CLK-WR)
interfaces.signals: external -> TOP: i_wr_en [level], i_wr_data, i_full_thr [static]; TOP -> external: o_full [level], o_full_thr [level], o_overflow [pulse]

interfaces.name: Read interface (CLK-RD)
interfaces.signals: external -> TOP: i_rd_en [level], i_empty_thr [static]; TOP -> external: o_rd_data, o_empty [level], o_empty_thr [level], o_underflow [pulse]

interfaces.name: Software reset (CLK-WR)
interfaces.signals: external -> TOP: i_rst_n_sw [level, active-low]; TOP -> external: o_sw_rst_busy [level]

interfaces.name: Gray pointers and software reset handshake
interfaces.active: u_wr -> u_rd (the read side answers with its pointer and acknowledge)
interfaces.signals: u_wr -> u_rd: o_wr_gray, o_req_wr (synchronized in u_rd); u_rd -> u_wr: o_rd_gray, o_ack_rd (synchronized in u_wr)

interfaces.name: Memory read port (data crosses without a synchronizer)
interfaces.signals: u_rd -> u_mem: o_mem_rd_addr; u_mem -> u_rd: i_mem_rd_data

interfaces.name: Clock and reset of the write side
Clock and reset of the read side

legend_note: The enclosing frame is the top module; blocks inside are its instances. The two clocks are asynchronous: the Gray pointers and the reset handshake cross through synchronizers inside u_wr and u_rd.
